notes: Perfect overlap on Scn9a regulation claims (C43-C48). Both evaluators accept the evidence for NOVA-dependent NMD regulation of Scn9a through cryptic exon E17a, validated by emetine and UPF1 knockdown experiments.

Perfect overlap on systematic cryptic NMD exon identification (C49-C51). Both evaluators praise this as a significant advance, with reviewers specifically noting the clever application of HITS-CLIP methodology.
Perfect overlap on Nova2+/- epilepsy phenotype (C14, C63-C66). Both evaluators accept the EEG evidence for spontaneous epilepsy in haploinsufficient mice without raising concerns.

High overlap on Dlg3 regulation (C35-C38 shared, plus C39-C41 in peer result). Both evaluators accept the experimental evidence for ~90% reduction in Dlg3 mRNA/protein and the NMD mechanism, though they group related claims differently.

Strong overlap on homeostatic regulation and seizure-induced changes (C10, C11, C15, C16, C53, C67, C68, C88, C116-C118). Both evaluators express uncertainty: LLM notes claims are inferential without direct causal demonstration; peer reviewers question whether pilocarpine effects reflect dynamic regulation or pathological damage.

Partial overlap on >200 NOVA-regulated transcripts (C4, C28). LLM finds evidence well-supported by multiple approaches; peer reviewers challenge the liberal cutoff (log2 0.3 = 1.25-fold) and request qRT-PCR validation to assess false-positive rates.

Partial overlap on NMD mechanism and cryptic exons (C6, C7, C42, C85). LLM finds convergent evidence strongly supports the mechanism; peer reviewers propose alternative interpretation that cryptic exon suppression may prevent spurious expression in non-neuronal cells rather than enable dynamic neuronal regulation.

Partial overlap on NOVA binding patterns (C5, C29, C34). Both evaluators accept HITS-CLIP data showing predominantly intronic binding. Peer reviewers praise the methodology as a clever application of genome-wide approaches.

Partial overlap on subcellular fractionation (C30-C32). Both evaluators accept the nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution data and distinct binding patterns in different compartments without raising concerns.
Partial overlap on NOVA background (C1-C3). Both evaluators accept established knowledge about NOVA as neuron-specific splicing regulator. This provides accepted context for the study.
Partial overlap on Dlg3 NMD mechanism details (C39-C41). Both evaluators accept the experimental validation of PTC-containing isoform, emetine treatment, and UPF1 knockdown results.

Partial overlap on seizure-induced NMD exon regulation (C10, C11, C53, C67). LLM finds RT-PCR and immunofluorescence data support activity-dependent regulation; peer reviewers question whether pilocarpine-induced changes reflect dynamic regulation or pathological effects.
Claims C54-C57, C60-C62 about minimal global splicing changes after seizure appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these control experiments.
Claims C70-C73 about Syngr3 3' UTR regulation appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this specific example.
Claims C74-C76 about GO analysis and functional distinctions between regulatory modes appear only in LLM results. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these bioinformatic analyses.
Claims C58-C59 about GO enrichment of seizure-regulated transcripts appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation.

Minimal overlap (C12 only) but conceptual alignment. Both evaluators express uncertainty about linking NOVA-regulated proteins to epilepsy mechanisms. LLM notes protein changes are inferred rather than directly measured; peer reviewers question the pilocarpine model's validity.
Claims C105-C106, C109-C110, C113 about nuclear-cytoplasmic coordination and cis-rearrangement models appear only in LLM results. LLM correctly identifies these as speculative mechanisms.
Claims C77-C84 about established NMD mechanisms from literature appear only in LLM results. These represent background context not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.

Minimal overlap (C89 only) on speculation about dynamic NOVA regulation. Both evaluators appropriately identify this as uncertain/speculative, with LLM noting limited evidence for GSK3 phosphorylation significance.
Claims C92-C93, C101 about other RNA binding proteins in epilepsy appear only in LLM results. These contextual citations are not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.
Claim C86 about evolutionary conservation appears only in LLM results. LLM correctly notes this references unpublished data and cannot be fully evaluated.

Minimal overlap (C33 only) on quantification that ~76% of NOVA CLIP tags are intronic. Both evaluators accept this as valid observation from HITS-CLIP data that motivated the mechanistic investigation.
Claims C104, C107-C108, C111, C114-C115 about methodological context and nuclear-cytoplasmic coordination precedents appear only in LLM results. Not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers.
